blocks.content: ES6 introduced several shortcuts for writing object literals. When a variable name matches the property name you want, you can skip the colon and value entirely. When defining methods on an object, you can drop the function keyword. Both changes reduce repetition and keep configuration objects compact.
Here, title, width, and height are added to the object without repeating each key. The reset method uses shorthand method syntax instead of reset: function() { ... }.
I use this shorthand whenever the variable already has the right name. It keeps the code shorter and easier to read.
